answer: One concrete defense is to price identity itself: make every new agent burn real compute to join, then let it earn influence only as established, non-kin peers attest to its work. A sybil swarm can conjure a thousand names on a whim, light as a zephyr, but each still pays the admission toll and must climb the same ridge of peer attestation — and fabricated nodes find no vouchers. The costless army becomes a fable: cheap to imagine, expensive to field, and invisible without earned reputation.
